# Shubham Kulkarni — Software Engineer, AI/ML (full profile, llms-full.txt)

> Shubham Kulkarni is a Software Engineer (AI/ML) at Arya Omnitalk Wireless Solutions (Arvind Group), Pune, India, since August 2025. He is the developer of VIDS (internally VIDES), an edge AI system for highway enforcement and incident detection, and a core engineer on TMCS, an NHAI ATMS-aligned highway incident-detection platform. He works across computer vision (YOLO, RT-DETR, ByteTrack, ANPR), TensorRT inference on NVIDIA Jetson and RTX GPU servers, real-time backend services, and RAG / agent applications. He led his team to AIR 1 (National Champion) at Smart India Hackathon 2023.

## Key numbers

- **VIDS:** 50,000+ unique vehicles a day across a ~100 km highway corridor at 90%+ ANPR accuracy; one gantry logged 620,000+ detections in 30 days on a single Jetson Orin Nano.
- **VIDS:** 7 models per node (6 TensorRT FP16 engines + PaddleOCR PP-OCRv4); ANPR and speed for every vehicle plus 16 violation and incident types.
- **VIDS scale-up:** 12 cameras with every detector on, on one RTX 5060 Ti GPU server (capacity depends on the hardware); 126 ms median detect-and-track per frame on a Jetson Orin Nano; operator alerts in under 150 ms.
- **TMCS:** 26 concurrent camera streams on one GPU server; 7 incident rules; 11 object classes; write-once SHA-256 evidence.
- **Tests:** 2,400+ automated tests across VIDS (2,100+) and TMCS (360).
- **Vehicle re-identification:** 150,000+ forensic queries a day, under 100 ms per search, 30× faster retrieval with FAISS IVF.
- **MHADA Pune Explorer (personal product):** 141K Google clicks and 1.56M impressions in 3 months (average position 4.9); 238K impressions in Google AI features; 34.8K citations in Microsoft Copilot answers; 108K visits in 30 days.

## Flagship work (Arya Omnitalk, proprietary)

- [VIDS case study](https://shubhamkulkarni.me/work/vides.html): Edge AI for highway enforcement and incidents. RTSP → GPU decode → YOLO (TensorRT FP16) → ByteTrack → ROI filtering → ANPR (plate detector + PP-OCRv4, 2-read consensus), helmet / triple riding, seatbelt, speed, lane rules and incident engines → per-vehicle finalizer → PostgreSQL → SSE / Socket.IO dashboard and an ATMS sync service. Every passing vehicle is recorded, not only violators. Scaled from a Jetson Orin Nano to 12 cameras on one RTX 5060 Ti by replacing per-camera RT-DETR engines with a shared engine pool.
- [TMCS case study](https://shubhamkulkarni.me/work/tmcs.html): Turns existing highway PTZ cameras into automatic incident detectors aligned with NHAI ATMS Standards (2023). YOLO + RT-DETR, time-based tracking, rider-aware pedestrian logic, night glare filtering, PTZ-aware analytics, write-once SHA-256 evidence. [Solution overview (PDF)](https://shubhamkulkarni.me/Asset/TMCS_Client_Solution_Overview.pdf)
- [Vehicle Re-Identification & Forensic Search](https://shubhamkulkarni.me/blog/vehicle-re-identification.html): OSNet + ResNet embeddings and FAISS IVF for cross-camera vehicle search (company work).

## VIDS architecture (detail)

- **Ingest:** RTSP streams decoded on the GPU with GStreamer; each camera keeps only its newest frame, so latency cannot drift behind real time.
- **Perception core:** custom-trained YOLO vehicle detector (7 classes: car, truck, bus, mini bus, auto-rickshaw, bike, tractor) in TensorRT FP16, ByteTrack tracking, then cheap ROI / lane / direction / size / track-quality filters before any expensive model runs.
- **Lane cameras (enforcement):** plate detector + PP-OCRv4 with blur penalty and 2-read consensus; helmet / triple riding and seatbelt models in parallel worker pools on bounded queues; speed from tracks with per-camera calibration; lane rules (overspeed, slow moving, wrong lane, wrong way, banned class). A detection finalizer joins all results per vehicle with a timeout.
- **Overview camera (incidents):** stopped vehicle, illegal parking, accident, queue, pedestrian, animal, debris (RT-DETR), pothole (daylight scan), low visibility. Fire and smoke detection is in development.
- **Output:** async DB writer to PostgreSQL (detections are never deleted, only moved through statuses enforced by a database trigger), SSE → Socket.IO operator dashboard (verify / discard with evidence), video-clip evidence encoded off the camera threads, USB relay alarm, and an ATMS sync service that sends each finished detection to the customer's ATMS.
- **Services:** backend AI service, Flask + Socket.IO dashboard and ATMS sync service share no code; they communicate only through the database, an SSE stream and an HTTP control API. Deployed with systemd on Jetson Orin Nano / NX and Linux GPU servers.
- **Scale-up story:** on 12 cameras, ~90% of frame time was spent waiting for the GPU lock because each overview camera ran its own RT-DETR engine. Fix: a shared RT-DETR engine pool (one per gantry plus a spare), newest-request-wins per camera, stale results (> 1 s) dropped, hung engines replaced automatically.
- **Field bug story:** a dog standing in a lane raised no alert. Causes: tracker score fusion prevented weak new tracks, and small objects shrank to ~14×20 px at a 640 px input. Fixes: same-day config hotfix, a ported time-aware tracker, automatic tiling (≤ 960 px tiles), and per-minute counters for every dropped detection.

## TMCS architecture (detail)

- **Pipeline:** ONVIF camera → RTSP ingest → PTZ preset scene gate → YOLO (vehicles) + RT-DETR (people, animals, debris) → ByteTrack with a time-aware Kalman filter → 7 time-based rules → incident lifecycle (one event per incident, with start and end) → write-once SHA-256 evidence → SSE hand-off to the control room.
- **Rules:** stopped vehicle, wrong-way driving, pedestrian on highway, animal on road, debris, queue / congestion, parked vehicle.
- **Engineering:** rider-aware occupant tagging, night glare filtering, tracks cleared and zones reloaded on every PTZ move, ONVIF circuit breaker for dead cameras, batched preset upsert (2,500 ms → under 10 ms), shared master VMS / ATCC database through a device-scoped view, tag-based RBAC re-checked on every request.
- **Measured:** tracking + rules p50 of 1.5 / 5.3 / 10.3 ms at 10 / 40 / 80 objects per frame (CPU dev machine, model time excluded).
